statements.statement: Every M arrow is monomorphic, and every endomorphism of an M object is the identity.
statements.argument: These are treated as the page's defining assumptions about M in the targeted arguments. No separate category named outside the page is asserted to satisfy them.

statements.place: After the starred two-row map, est injective par (i)(ii)
statements.statement: For a fixed representative D-prime, u -> u(D-prime) injects Hom_M(D-prime,D) into the subobjects of D.
statements.argument: Condition (i) makes every arrow a monomorphism and hence a subobject representative. If u and v define the same subobject, the definition of equal subobjects gives an isomorphism a:D-prime -> D-prime with u=v a. Condition (ii) makes a the identity. Thus u=v.
statements.outcome: Passed for the usual definition of subobject as a monomorphism modulo isomorphism of its domain.

statements.place: Inserted Il est en fait ordonné, grâce à (ii)
statements.statement: The usual reachability preorder on isomorphism classes of objects is an order.
statements.argument: Use [A]<= [B] when a morphism A->B exists. Identities and composition give reflexivity and transitivity. If f:A->B and g:B->A exist, (ii) gives gf=id_A and fg=id_B. Hence f and g are inverse isomorphisms, so the two classes are equal. The relation is independent of representatives by conjugating with isomorphisms.
statements.outcome: Passed for the natural reachability relation on classes; this condition on the relation is explicit in the check.

statements.place: Lower paragraph, l'ens ordonné ... est défini à isom unique près; stronger literal interpretation
statements.statement: Conditions (i) and (ii) force uniqueness among all abstract ordered-set isomorphisms between the resulting subobject orders.
statements.argument: Counterexample internal to the page's hypotheses: take objects A,B, their identities, two distinct arrows f,g:A->B, and no other arrows. Both f and g are monic because each Hom(X,A) has at most one element; the only endomorphisms are identities. Sub(B) consists of the distinct incomparable subobjects [f],[g] below [id_B]. Its automorphism exchanging [f] and [g] is nontrivial. Thus uniqueness among arbitrary order isomorphisms does not follow.
statements.outcome: Refuted only for this explicitly stronger interpretation, not attributed as the author's intended meaning. The valid canonical-transport statement is 007-CANONICAL-TRANSPORT.

statements.place: Lower paragraph, representative D_n and its ordered set of subobjects
statements.statement: Isomorphic representatives are joined by a unique M-isomorphism; its transport gives a distinguished order isomorphism of their subobject orders.
statements.argument: If a,b:A->B are isomorphisms, b^{-1}a is an endomorphism of A, so (ii) gives b^{-1}a=id and a=b. Composition with this unique isomorphism sends each monomorphism into A to a monomorphism into B, respects the subobject equivalence and factorization order, and has inverse induced by the inverse isomorphism. This proves canonical transport, without claiming that every abstract order isomorphism arises in this way.
statements.outcome: Passed. This is the precise interpretation under which the page's unique-isomorphism wording is justified by (ii).
